quick_skim.title: Reading Across Space, Time and Frequencies: Tensor Decomposition of SEEG Signals to Support Epileptogenic Zone Definition
quick_skim.abstract: Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) is an invasive technique used in the presurgical evaluation of drug-resistant epilepsy to support the localization of the Epileptogenic Zone (EZ). SEEG data are particularly complex to analyze, as they include hundreds of components, named channels, each associated with a different brain site, with interactions varying in both time and frequency. In this study, we propose a new framework for SEEG analysis, based on the Canonical Polyadic (CP) decomposition, to extract the latent modes underlying seizure generation. We model SEEG signals as a third-order tensor (channel x time x frequency), and factorize the tensor into rank-1 factors. We then exploit the channel-specific factor as an unsupervised feature set for identifying the EZ. The framework is validated on SEEG-recorded seizures from 35 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. The results show that the joint combination of multiple frequency bands significantly enhances classification performance.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Stereo-EEG analysis is hard because hundreds of channels interact across time and frequency. The authors model SEEG as a channel-by-time-by-frequency tensor and apply canonical polyadic decomposition, extracting latent modes and channel signatures that support epileptogenic zone definition.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 立体脑电信号包含数百个通道且在时间与频率上交互复杂，传统分析难以刻画其潜在结构。作者提出基于规范多项式分解的分析框架，将脑电建模为通道×时间×频率的三阶张量并分解为秩一因子，从通道签名中提取与致痫区相关的潜在模式。实验表明该分解能够刻画癫痫发生过程的时空频耦合结构并辅助致痫区定位。该工作为多维度脑电特征编码提供了可解释的张量建模范式。

quick_skim.title: Temporal Contrastive Alignment of EEG and Naturalistic Video Only Beats Linear Decoding On In-Sample Stimuli
quick_skim.abstract: Neural tracking, the temporal alignment between a continuous stimulus and the elicited brain response, enables decoding of attention from electroencephalography (EEG), yet its application to naturalistic video remains largely unexplored and mainly relies on linear canonical correlation analysis (CCA). We investigate whether a temporal contrastive model, pairing pretrained VideoMAE features with a lightweight EEG encoder trained on a correlation-based InfoNCE objective, can strengthen EEG-video alignment. Benchmarked against CCA under three generalization regimes, the model outperforms CCA across subjects (leave-one-subject-out), matches it within the stimulus manifold (leave-video-segment-out), and falls behind CCA when extrapolating to entirely novel videos (leave-one-video-out). Because this advantage appears only for seen stimuli, we probe its basis: a sham control shows that a high accuracy does not certify genuine alignment, as a synthesized correspondence fit to the seen stimuli can reproduce it without genuine temporal alignment in the training pairs. This does not preclude practical use: on a downstream attention-decoding task with seen stimuli, the model remains better than CCA since the decoding only requires a strong statistical coupling, regardless of whether that coupling is physiologically meaningful. Using a group-averaged EEG reference, we further show that genuine, generalizable coupling is nonetheless learned, only buried in the noise of single-subject EEG. These results indicate that progress hinges on data scale, diversity, and single-subject denoising.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对自然视频下脑电神经跟踪研究不足且主要依赖线性典型相关分析的问题，作者提出时间对比对齐模型，将预训练VideoMAE特征与轻量脑电编码器通过相关式InfoNCE目标联合训练。在三种泛化设置下与CCA比较，跨被试留一设置优于CCA，留视频片段设置持平，样本内刺激略逊。结果表明对比式表征可提升跨被试对齐，但泛化到新刺激仍受限。
